gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Gugi stands tall and bold, its lowercase nearly touching the capitals and its curves matching the stems. And Noto Sans Khmer, a sans-serif, carries a long block of text with generous openings and small letters that stand proud.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Gugi pairs lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals with curves and stems moving in lockstep, giving headings a drawn-in-one-line look. Then Noto Sans Khojki sits beneath it, with wide exits that let light through and a large eye on every e.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Blunt, bold and oddly tidy, Gugi draws every glyph with a single-width stroke and lowercase that climbs close to the capitals. Noto Sans Khudawadi follows, low in contrast, its rounds left unlatched.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-kr: Noto Sans KR reads openly, with generous gaps in its curves, stubby ascenders and descenders, and a big x-height. Gugi, though, brings the pair its strongest quality: a heavy, thick-only outline that makes headings unmistakable.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-lao: Gugi's line width never swells or tapers, and its terminals are cut open so the counters flow outward. Noto Sans Lao handles the quieter work, pushing its x-height well above the usual so the sans-serif text stays easy to follow.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped makes words read as solid blocks rather than skylines, its bowls left unfinished on one side. Gugi supplies the strongest quality here, an uninterrupted monoline stroke that gives the heading its bold, distinctive voice.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha reads with wide-open curves and a lowercase that has the stature of cast iron capitals. Gugi does the shouting, with one pen line holding its width throughout, while the sans below does the steady talking.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Gugi draws everything in a single track width, like a neon sign tube, with tall lowercase nearly reaching the capitals. Noto Sans Limbu sits beside it with gaping curves and tall-bodied small letters, so the two feel like close relatives of different volumes.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Heavy, bold and instantly distinctive, Gugi holds one hum of weight in every letter, with its terminals cut open. Noto Sans Lisu, a sans-serif, softens things with tiny gaps below its ascenders.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-lydian: A flat, unvarying line weight in every letter is the first thing you notice about Gugi, which also lifts its lowercase nearly to capital height. And Noto Sans Lydian follows with capitals barely taller than its lowercase and openings as wide as a sprung paper clip.
